messages:
maria: quick q — thinking about shrinking the surface area for service auth between runtime components (ingress/router/worker). current model: route-level API keys + operator tokens + optional proxy creds. feels... leaky and hard to reason about. any objections to a bold contraction: one signed short-lived operator token per request path, plus resource-intent tags for policy?

james: +1 on reducing variants. can you sketch failure modes? especially cross-tenant routing and auditability.

maria: sure. main goals: 1) least-privilege per hop, 2) simple runtime checks (no multi-lookup authz), 3) strong audit trail. tradeoffs: we lose the ability to hand out long-lived route-specific API keys to third-parties (ok for internal). also need token minting infra and latency considerations.

alex: latency is my main worry. mint-per-request adds crypto and network hops. can we cache signed tokens per route+origins for short window? e.g., 30s cache with refresh. also: what about third-party webhooks that can't do token exchange?

maria: yes cache at router layer for same origin+path (no priv escalation). 30s is a good starting point. for external webhooks we could keep a compatibility layer that maps legacy API keys to a token broker flow, rate-limited and flagged in audit.

sophia: how do intent tags look? example pls.

maria: intent tags = strings in token claims: "intent:invoke-model;route:/v1/complete;dataset:user-uploads". policy engine checks intent+route+tenant. simplifies policy evaluation to single check.

james: sounds good. but RBAC still useful for admin operations. propose hybrid: tokens for runtime RPCs (machine-to-machine), RBAC for control-plane ops. keep APIs separate.

alex: agree. also add a token fallback for retries: if signed token validation fails (edge desync), fallback to allow a monitored legacy key for 10s while control-plane syncs. emit metric and alert.

maria: good call. also want to avoid adding too many token types. plan: (A) request-scoped signed operator token (primary), (B) admin RBAC tokens (long-lived service keys with scoping), (C) legacy compatibility broker.

sophia: what about key rotation and compromise blast radius?

maria: operator tokens are short-lived and signed by KMS-managed key. rotation is implicit. admin keys rotate per current ops playbook (vault-backed). broker keys get extra monitoring.

security-bot: Note: add automated revocation hook to the broker for suspected compromise (ticket -> revoke mapping).

james: action items: 1) design token minting flow + caching (alex), 2) policy mapping spec for intent tags -> RBAC equivalence (sophia), 3) compatibility broker design + revocation hooks (maria).

alex: i'll prototype a node service minting JWTs with ed25519 and 30s TTL + in-process cache. will push a quick PoC by EOD tomorrow.
sophia: will draft policy spec and example rules: allow invoke-model if intent==invoke-model && tenant in allowedTenants.
maria: thanks. if we agree on this contraction i'll open an RFC PR documenting failure modes, latency budget, and migration plan for external customers.
james: 👍 small follow-up: add metrics for token mint latency, cache hit rate, broker fallback count.
maria: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
